label_treatment.why: Disgust is negative but has no dependable arousal direction, so its quadrant is a choice rather than a reading. Included here to retain data; note the other evaluation excludes it.

verdict: Raw agreement 33.3%, Cohen's kappa 0.1206 (slight). But the reference model is degenerate on radio: it assigns one quadrant to 74% of clips. On CREMA-D it works normally (81.7% vs a 58.3% baseline, largest class 61%), so the failure is domain transfer in the *reference*, not evidence about our scoring. This comparison cannot adjudicate either way - it is reported because the attempt was made, not because it settles anything.
why_kappa: Raw agreement is misleading here: both models over-produce one or two quadrants, so a large share of agreement happens by accident. Kappa subtracts the agreement expected from the marginal distributions.
